Search Attack ID

Resolve the Attack ID from a FortiWeb block page to its attack-log entry, investigate it field by field (optionally with Scout, the AI assistant), and build, save and insert a narrowly scoped exception.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsprotection.view advisor.use protection.edit protection.apply
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → Operations → WAF → Search Attack ID (URL /waf/attack-search/)

What is it?#

When FortiWeb blocks a request, the block page shows the caller an Attack ID such as id-fweb-01-000000004117. Search Attack ID turns that reference into the attack-log entry it points to and puts the whole triage on one page: what was blocked and why, whether it looks like a false positive, and — if it is — the exception that would let it through, written onto the appliance in two deliberate steps.

What does it do?#

  • Lookup — parses the reference, finds the appliance from it, and searches that appliance's attack log for the MSG ID. On a miss it shows the newest ten entries, so you can tell a stale ID from a broken feed.
  • Profile column — for each row, the Web Protection Profile the policy binds right now and whether it is shared with other policies.
  • Entry panel — click a row for the full entry. Each field has Explain this field (local analysis, no external lookups) and, when Scout (the AI assistant) is on, Ask the AI about this field.
  • Analyze with AI — Scout judges the entry (false-positive, true-attack or uncertain, plus a risk) and may draft an exception you Accept, adapt or Reject.
  • Build an exception — SATOM proposes the exception type and the fields to scope it by; Preview the exception, then Save as draft.
  • Insert into the appliance — Preview the exact request, then Insert it into the appliance now.

Requirements#

  • The FortiWeb that blocked the request is registered in SATOM and visible to you. The device part of the reference is matched to the appliance name (case-insensitive), then to its management address.
  • SATOM can log in to the appliance's GUI to read its attack log.
  • For the AI functions: Scout, the AI assistant (called AI Advisor until 2026-10-14), is enabled with a working provider (see Scout).

No current device is needed; the page works from the reference.

Permissions#

Action Needs Without it
Search, view entries, Explain this field, exception type suggestions, Preview the exception The legacy view permission — any granular view key, for example protection.view or monitoring.view The page answers 403 Forbidden
Analyze with AI, Ask the AI about this field advisor.use The AI buttons are not shown
Save as draft, Accept, Reject, insert target list, Preview the exact request, Insert it into the appliance now config_write — from protection.edit, protection.apply or any other *.edit / *.apply key The request is refused with 403 Forbidden

Accept and Reject of an AI-drafted exception also require that you can see the device the proposal is for (current ADOM, maintenance rules).

The AI buttons are drawn only when Scout is enabled on this node and you hold advisor.use; when Scout is switched off the panel says Scout, the AI assistant, is switched off (Settings → Scout). You can still build an exception by hand below.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the AI buttons are shown only to users with advisor.use, and rejecting a proposal for a device you cannot see is refused, as accepting already was.

How to use#

Find the entry#

  1. Open Operations → WAF → Search Attack ID.
  2. Paste the reference into Attack ID. The full id-<device>-<number> form, the bare MSG ID, or the number without leading zeros all work.
  3. Leave Appliance on From the ID, or pick the appliance explicitly (for example for a reference minted before a rename).
  4. Click Search.

The result badge shows the MSG ID, the appliance and the number of matches. The table lists Date/Time, MSG ID, Attack Type, Sub Type, Policy, Web Protection Profile, Source IP, Destination IP and Action.

In the Web Protection Profile column a green badge means the policy owns the profile alone; an amber badge reads shared with ; unknown means SATOM could not read the bindings; policy not on device means the policy was renamed or removed since the entry was logged.

Investigate one entry#

  1. Click a row (or Open details). The panel opens with the main fields of the entry; the full entry is below.
  2. Click the info icon on a field for a local explanation of the value and, for addresses, hosts and user agents, how often the same value appears in the last 100 log entries.
  3. Click the chat icon to ask Scout about that field. Type a follow-up and press Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on a Mac); follow-ups continue the same conversation. This path answers questions only — it never drafts an exception.

Ask Scout for a verdict#

  1. In AI investigation click Analyze with AI. SATOM re-reads the entry from the appliance and sends it to Scout.
  2. Read the verdict, risk and reasoning. If Scout judged a false positive at low or medium risk, a Drafted exception card follows.
  3. Optionally edit Raw payload — edit to adapt it before accepting, then click Accept (stores a draft) or Reject (recorded, not erased).

If the draft contradicts Scout's own verdict, the card is headed in red: Scout drafted an exception that contradicts its own judgement.

Build the exception yourself#

  1. In Build an exception, check the proposed type and the ticked scope fields. Each tick carries the reason it was chosen; required fields are always included.
  2. Click Preview the exception to see the route, breadth and the exact body. Optionally edit Raw payload — edit to adapt it.
  3. If Scout judged the entry true-attack, or the risk high or unacceptable, write a justification (at least 20 characters).
  4. If the profile is shared or template-managed, the panel says This profile cannot take the exception as it stands. Tick Clone the profile and re-bind the policy to let SATOM clone it under the Naming pattern and re-bind the Server Policy — a real write to the appliance.
  5. Click Save as draft. The message reads Carve-out saved as a draft.

Insert it into the appliance#

  1. In Insert into the appliance, choose Which object on the device it goes into; tick Create the container if it does not exist where offered.
  2. Click Preview the exact request. Nothing is written.
  3. Click Insert it into the appliance now. This writes to a live WAF. It takes effect immediately.

The saved draft is also listed on Exceptions & Signature, where it can be versioned, deployed or deleted.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Attack ID Reference from the block page, or the bare MSG ID Yes id-fweb-01-000000004117, 4117
Appliance Override the appliance resolved from the reference No fweb-01
Question Free text for Ask the AI about this field (max 600 characters) No Is this user agent a known scanner?
Justification Required when contradicting Scout's verdict 20+ characters when required Partner integration sends this payload by design

Example#

🧪Example — Partner callback blocked as SQL injection

A partner reports a block page with id-fweb-01-000000004117. The operator searches it, sees signature detection on policy shop-api with profile wpp-shop shared with shop-www. Analyze with AI returns false-positive / low. The operator keeps the proposed Signature Exception (per-id) scoped to the URL, ticks Clone the profile and re-bind the policy, saves the draft, previews the exact request and inserts it. Only shop-api is affected.

Result#

  • Every search (hit or miss), field explanation, AI question (with the question text), analysis, save, accept, reject and insert is written to the Audit log. Accepting records both the proposed and the approved payload.
  • Save as draft and Accept store a carve-out in SATOM; only the guided clone (when ticked) and Insert it into the appliance now write to the device.

Troubleshooting#

"Unrecognised attack ID. Expected "id--" as shown on the block page, or the bare numeric MSG ID."#

Solution — paste the reference exactly as shown, or only its number.

"No appliance in SATOM is named "". Pick the device explicitly, or add it under Appliances."#

Possible causes — the appliance was renamed, or is not registered or not visible to you.

Solution — choose it in Appliance, or register it in Appliances.

"This reference does not name a device, so pick the appliance to search."#

Solution — you searched a bare MSG ID; select the Appliance.

"Attack-log feed unavailable: …"#

Possible causes — SATOM cannot log in to the appliance GUI or reach it.

Solution — check reachability and credentials of the appliance.

"no match" and a list of recent entries#

Possible causes — the entry has aged out of the log, or the wrong appliance was searched.

Solution — compare with the recent entries shown; if the ID is older than all of them it has rotated out.

"MSG ID is no longer in 's attack log…"#

Solution — the entry aged out between the search and the action; search again or author the exception on Exceptions & Signature.

"Scout, the AI assistant, is switched off (Settings → Scout)."#

Solution — ask an administrator to enable Scout and a provider (Settings → System → Scout).

"Scout judged this … Authoring an exception anyway may well be right — but write down why…"#

Solution — enter a justification of at least 20 characters and save again.

"Signature set "" already holds 128/128 exception entries — FortiWeb rejects more. Remove one first."#

Solution — free an entry in that signature set, or choose another target.

Advanced Internals
  • Every action re-reads the entry from the appliance by MSG ID; SATOM never trusts a log row sent by the browser.
  • Explain this field uses no WHOIS, geolocation or threat feeds; the only network call is an optional reverse-DNS lookup through the SATOM host's resolver.
  • Shared-profile detection reads the policy bindings off the device. When they cannot be read, the state is unknown and is treated like shared. The push re-checks scope and refuses (403) when the profile still needs a clone.
  • AI exchanges are kept as Scout conversations; a proposal drafted during a field question is dismissed automatically.
